name: compile

methods.name: __init__
methods.summary: Wrap `model` for cached graph-capture execution.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
The compute unit to compile.  Stored unwrapped so
attribute access falls through to it.

parameters.name: dynamic
parameters.description:
Declare that this module will be called with **varying batch
sizes**.  Default `False`.  Variable batch is always handled by
**per-shape static caching** — each distinct input shape compiles its
own executable, cached and reused — which works for every model and
never recompiles for a shape already seen.  A *single* executable
shared across batch sizes (a symbolic batch axis) is **not** offered
automatically: Apple's MPSGraph aborts (uncatchably) the moment a
graph materialises a constant carrying the symbolic axis — scalar
arithmetic (`x * 0.5`), `reshape` / `flatten`, reductions,
convolutions and attention all trip it, i.e. essentially every real
model.  The narrow class that *is* safe (pure `linear` /
activation / `softmax` / `layer_norm` / `embedding` graphs) can
opt in to the experimental symbolic path with the
`LUCID_COMPILE_DYNAMIC=1` environment variable; without it
`dynamic=True` is exactly the safe per-shape static behaviour.

methods.name: model
methods.summary: The wrapped `nn.Module` (or duck-typed callable wrapper).

methods.name: dynamic
methods.summary: Whether `dynamic=True` (variable batch) was requested.
methods.extended:
This is the *requested* flag.  By default it selects robust per-shape
static caching; a single symbolic-batch executable is used only when the
experimental `LUCID_COMPILE_DYNAMIC=1` opt-in is also set.

methods.name: training
methods.summary: Mirrors the inner model's `training` flag (cache-invalidating).

methods.name: parameters
methods.summary: Delegate to `model.parameters` so optimizers see the live tensors.

methods.name: named_parameters
methods.summary: Delegate to `model.named_parameters` (no recompile, read-only).

methods.name: buffers
methods.summary: Delegate to `model.buffers`; buffers are pinned trace constants.

methods.name: state_dict
methods.signature: state_dict(destination: dict[str, Tensor] | None = None, prefix: str = '', keep_vars: bool = False)
methods.summary: Delegate to `model.state_dict` — the cache holds no separate state.

methods.name: load_state_dict
methods.signature: load_state_dict(state_dict: dict[str, Tensor], strict: bool = True, assign: bool = False)
methods.summary: Forward to `model.load_state_dict` and **drop the cache**.
methods.extended:
Loading new weights doesn't change the graph topology, but
captured tensor *identities* may shift (e.g. when the loader
replaces parameter storage in-place); clearing the cache is
the safe default so the next call traces against the new
state.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description:
Mapping from parameter / buffer name to weight tensor —
passed straight through to the wrapped model's
`load_state_dict`.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description:
When `True`, mismatched keys raise; when `False`,
missing / unexpected entries are silently ignored
(matches the underlying module's contract).

parameters.name: assign
parameters.description:
When `True`, replace parameter storage by reference
instead of copying into the existing tensors.  Useful for
checkpoint loading where the new tensors are already on
the correct device.

returns.description:
The wrapped model's `load_state_dict` return value
(typically a `NamedTuple` of missing / unexpected
keys).

methods.name: train
methods.summary: Flip training mode; **clears the cache** since BN / Dropout diverge.

methods.name: eval
methods.summary: Shorthand for `self.train(False)`; also clears the cache.

methods.name: to
methods.summary: Forward to `model.to` and **drop the cache**.
methods.extended:
Placeholders inside the cached MPSGraph executables are
device-locked, so any device or dtype move invalidates every
entry.

methods.name: cache_info
methods.summary: Snapshot the cache state for tests + telemetry.

returns.description:
Four fields:

* `entries` (int) — number of cached executables.
* `keys` (tuple[CacheKey]) — every signature that
  currently has a compiled executable.
* `eager_only` (tuple[CacheKey]) — signatures that
  failed to compile and were blacklisted; future calls
  with these signatures route straight to eager.  A call
  that needed gradients is here too, under its key with
  `grad=True`.
* `n_calls` (dict[CacheKey, int]) — per-signature call
  counter, useful for spotting hot signatures.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> model = nn.Linear(8, 4).to("metal")
>>> compiled = lucid.compile(model)
>>> x1 = lucid.randn(2, 8, device="metal")
>>> x2 = lucid.randn(5, 8, device="metal")
>>> with lucid.no_grad():
...     _ = compiled(x1); _ = compiled(x2)
>>> info = compiled.cache_info()
>>> info["entries"]                 # one slot per unique signature
2

methods.name: timing
methods.summary: Per-signature compile + run cost breakdown.

returns.description:
One entry per cached signature with fields `key`
(CacheKey), `compile_ms` (float — first-call compile
cost), `last_run_ms` (float — most recent execution
time), and `n_hits` (int — total runs of this entry).
Useful to verify the cache amortises compile cost over
subsequent calls.

methods.name: clear_cache
methods.summary: Drop every cached executable + retry blacklist + call counter.
methods.extended:
Invalidates the param-fingerprint cache and the lazy training
step callables too, so the next call re-fingerprints the
model.  Called automatically by `train` / `eval`
/ `to` / `load_state_dict` — direct user calls
are useful only when forcing a recompile after manual
parameter buffer surgery.

methods.name: step
methods.signature: step(args: object = (), loss_fn: Callable[..., Tensor] | None)
methods.summary: Run one compiled training step.
methods.extended:
Equivalent to:

step_fn = make_step(self.model, loss_fn)
    loss = step_fn(*args)

but the underlying `make_step` callable is cached on this
`CompiledModule` so repeated training-step calls with
the same loss function share the fwd+bwd executable.  The
returned scalar loss tensor carries a `grad_fn` — calling
`loss.backward()` populates `.grad` on every parameter
from the cached gradient outputs.

parameters.name: *args
parameters.description:
`(model_input, *extra_loss_inputs)` — the same positional
tuple `make_step` expects.  Typically `(x, target)`.

parameters.name: loss_fn
parameters.description:
`loss_fn(model_output, *extra_inputs) -> Tensor` scalar
loss.  Keyed by object identity for caching; pass the same
function object across iterations to hit the cache.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> import lucid.nn.functional as F
>>> cm = lucid.compile(nn.Linear(8, 3).to("metal"))
>>> opt = lucid.optim.SGD(cm.parameters(), lr=0.1)
>>> loader = [
...     (lucid.randn(4, 8, device="metal"), lucid.randint(0, 3, (4,), device="metal"))
...     for _ in range(2)
... ]
>>> for x, t in loader:
...     opt.zero_grad()
...     loss = cm.step(x, t, loss_fn=F.cross_entropy)
...     loss.backward()
...     opt.step()

methods.name: graph_dump
methods.summary: Return a JSON view of the captured trace(s).
methods.extended:
Without `key`: a JSON list of `{sig, graph}` pairs covering
every cached signature.  With `key`: just the graph string
for that one signature.

Useful for offline debugging — pipe the result through
`tools/inspect_trace.py` (Phase 1.6 deliverable) or
diff two consecutive compiles to see what changed.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description:
When supplied, dump only the trace for that signature.
When `None` (default), dump every cached signature in
one combined JSON array.

returns.description:
JSON-encoded trace dump.  Empty string when `key` was
provided but no entry matches.

see_also.name: cache_info
see_also.description: structural snapshot of every cached signature.

methods.name: __call__
methods.summary: Route the call through the per-signature executable cache.
methods.extended:
On cache hit: bind the input tensors to the cached
executable's feed slots, run, and re-pack the flat output
list into the user's return structure (Tensor / tuple / dict
/ dataclass).  On miss: trace, compile, store, run — and on
compile failure mark the signature `eager_only` so future
calls skip the recompile attempt.  Under grad mode, a call
that reads a tensor requiring grad runs eagerly, so its result
is differentiable (see the class Notes).

parameters.name: *args
parameters.description:
Whatever the wrapped model's `forward` accepts.  Only
positional `Tensor` arguments become executable
feeds; non-tensor positionals (and any keyword arguments)
force the call to eager (today's compile pipeline doesn't
bind kwargs by name).

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Whatever the wrapped model's `forward` accepts.  Only
positional `Tensor` arguments become executable
feeds; non-tensor positionals (and any keyword arguments)
force the call to eager (today's compile pipeline doesn't
bind kwargs by name).

returns.description:
Same structure the underlying `model(*args, **kwargs)`
produces — Tensor, tuple, dataclass, etc.

notes:
`CompiledModule[**P, R]` carries the wrapped callable's
signature, so this returns `R` (the model's `forward`
return type) instead of `object`.  The runtime is
signature-agnostic; the static surface mirrors what
`lucid.compile` captured from its `Callable[P, R]`
argument.

members.signature: DiagnosisReport(total_ops: int, registered: list[OpInfo], grad_sinks: list[OpInfo], uncovered: list[OpInfo], recommendation: str)

methods.name: __str__
methods.summary: Render a short human-readable summary.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(total_ops: int, registered: list[OpInfo], grad_sinks: list[OpInfo], uncovered: list[OpInfo], recommendation: str)
methods.summary: Wrap `fn` so it satisfies the `nn.Module` contract.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description:
The plain callable the user passed to `compile`.
Stored unwrapped; invoked verbatim on every forward.

members.extended:
Holds three parallel buckets of `OpInfo` plus a one-line
`recommendation`.  The class is immutable; `__str__` renders a
short human-readable summary suitable for logs.

attributes.name: total_ops
attributes.description: Sum of every op occurrence in the trace.

attributes.name: registered
attributes.description: Ops with a registered `VjpEmitter` — real gradient.

attributes.name: grad_sinks
attributes.description:
Ops in the walker's `no_grad_ops` set — gradient flow stops
here by design (not a fallback).

attributes.name: uncovered
attributes.description:
Ops without an emitter and not in the sink set — will trigger
soft-fallback to MPSGraph autograd (or hard-fail under
`LUCID_MANUAL_VJP_REQUIRE=1`).

members.name: OpInfo
members.signature: OpInfo(name: str, count: int, sample_shape: tuple[int, ...] | None, sample_dtype: str | None)

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(name: str, count: int, sample_shape: tuple[int, ...] | None, sample_dtype: str | None)
methods.summary: Wrap `fn` so it satisfies the `nn.Module` contract.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description:
The plain callable the user passed to `compile`.
Stored unwrapped; invoked verbatim on every forward.

members.extended:
A single `OpInfo` aggregates *all* nodes in the trace with
the same op name into one record (`count` is the number of
occurrences; `sample_shape` / `sample_dtype` are taken from the
first occurrence's primary output, useful when reporting a coverage
gap).

attributes.name: count
attributes.description: Number of times the op appears in the captured trace.

attributes.name: sample_shape
attributes.description:
Shape of the first occurrence's primary output, or `None` if
the op produces no outputs (rare; defensive fallback).

attributes.name: sample_dtype
attributes.description:
Dtype name of the first occurrence's primary output
(`"float32"` / `"int64"` / ...) — uses
`lucid._C.engine.Dtype.name`.

members.name: diagnose
members.extended:
Runs `fn` once inside a `_tracing` context to capture the
op DAG, then classifies every op against the registry exposed by
`vjp_registration_status` (C++ engine binding).  Does
**not** compile or execute the captured graph — purely
introspective, runs in milliseconds even for large models.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description:
Any callable that returns a `Tensor` (or a tuple of
them).  An `nn.Module` instance works because
`Module.__call__` is the callable.

parameters.name: *example_inputs
parameters.description:
Positional arguments forwarded to `fn`.  Their concrete
shape / dtype are recorded into the trace, so the diagnosis
reflects exactly what would be compiled for these inputs.

returns.description:
Three-bucket classification + recommendation string.  Inspect
`.uncovered` to see which ops will fall back, or print
`str(report)` for a quick log line.

examples:
>>> import lucid, lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.compile import diagnose
>>> model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 4))
>>> print(diagnose(model, lucid.zeros(2, 8)))
Diagnosis: 5 op(s) total ...
100% manual VJP coverage — no fallback expected ...

see_also.name: path that consults the same registry under the hood.

members.name: compiled_decode_step
members.signature: compiled_decode_step(forward_fn: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], static_cache: StaticCache | EncoderDecoderCache)
members.summary: Return a `step(input_ids, cache_position)` running one compiled decode.

parameters.name: forward_fn
parameters.description:
`forward_fn(input_ids, cache_position) -> output` — one decode forward
that reads/writes `static_cache` internally (e.g. a model's
single-token path).  Must return a single Tensor (the decode logits /
hidden state).

parameters.name: static_cache
parameters.description:
The cache whose per-layer self-attention buffers `forward_fn` writes
via `lucid.index_copy`.  Its buffers are rolled forward in place.

returns.description:
`step(input_ids, cache_position) -> Tensor`.  `input_ids` is the new
token(s); `cache_position` is a fixed-shape `(T,)` int64 Tensor of
absolute write indices.  On a signature miss it (re)traces + compiles;
otherwise it is a pure run + buffer write-back.  Falls back to a plain
eager `forward_fn` call if the decode graph cannot be compiled, and
under grad mode when the step needs gradients (see the module notes).

members.name: compiled_step
members.signature: compiled_step(model: Module, x: Tensor, loss_fn: Callable[[Tensor], Tensor])
members.summary: Run one compiled training step: forward + backward + grad accumulation.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Module whose `forward(x)` produces the model output.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Input tensor (single forward pass).

parameters.name: loss_fn
parameters.description: Maps `model(x)` → scalar loss tensor.  Typical: `lambda y: F.cross_entropy(y, target)`.

returns.description:
The loss (compiled result, with no graph: its backward has run).
Its gradients are added into `.grad` as `loss.backward()` adds
them — of each parameter that requires grad, of a loss weight
`loss_fn` reads, and of `x` and the graph behind it when `x`
requires grad.  Then run the optimizer.

raises.description:
A gradient passes through a custom `Function`, whose `backward`
the executable cannot run (`make_step` runs such a step eagerly).

examples:
>>> import lucid, lucid.nn as nn, lucid.nn.functional as F
>>> import lucid.optim as optim
>>> from lucid.compile._entry.function import compiled_step
>>> model = nn.Linear(8, 4).to('metal')
>>> opt = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
>>> for batch in batches:
...     opt.zero_grad()
...     loss = compiled_step(model, batch.x,
...                          lambda y: F.cross_entropy(y, batch.target))
...     opt.step()
notes:
Parameters on the CPU have nothing to compile (Metal only): the step runs
eagerly, with a one-time `CompileFallbackWarning`.

The trace is captured in the caller's grad mode and fresh on every call;
cache integration (compile-or-cached) lives in Phase 1.4's
`CompiledModule`.

Phase 1.3 acceptance: `ResNet-18 + CE + SGD, 5 steps`, param
drift < 5e-3 vs eager.

cache so the compile cost amortises.

members.name: fused_step
members.signature: fused_step(model: Module, loss_fn: Callable[..., Tensor], optimizer: Optimizer, grad_scaler: GradScaler | None = None)
members.summary: Return a callable that runs one fused training step.
members.extended:
The first call traces `model(*x); loss_fn(out, *targets)` and the
optimizer update once under a single `Tracer`, plumbs the
ghost-grad placeholders, and compiles the resulting graph into one
`MPSGraphExecutable` that runs forward + loss + backward (via
MPSGraph autodiff) + optimizer update in a single submission.
Subsequent calls reuse the cached executable.

The step matches an eager `zero_grad(); loss.backward();
optimizer.step()` loop: a parameter the loss does not depend on, or
one with `requires_grad=False`, gets no gradient and is left
untouched (state and step count included), and every hyper-parameter
is read from `optimizer.param_groups` on each call, so LR
schedulers work.  `optimizer.state_dict()` /
`load_state_dict()` checkpoint the state this step updates (the
compiled optimizer owns it from `fused_step(...)` on — see
`compile_optimizer`).

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
The trainable `nn.Module`.  Parameters from
`optimizer.param_groups` must reference these tensors.

parameters.name: loss_fn
parameters.description:
Scalar-loss-returning callable invoked as
`loss_fn(model_output, *targets)`.  Captured by identity in
the trace, so passing a fresh closure each call defeats the
cache.

parameters.name: optimizer
parameters.description:
Any optimizer `compile_optimizer` supports, with any
number of parameter groups.

parameters.name: grad_scaler
parameters.description:
When provided and enabled, the fused step replicates the
eager `lucid.amp.GradScaler` contract inside the
compiled executable (scales loss before backward, unscales
gradients in F32, guards updates with `where(found_inf, old, new)`,
and reads `found_inf` back to drive `scaler.update()`).

returns.description:
A callable `step(*args)` where `args` is
`(model_input, *loss_targets)`.  Returns the scalar loss
`Tensor` from the just-completed step.

raises.description:
On the first call, when no parameter both requires grad and
reaches the loss (there would be nothing to step).  On any call
given a tensor that requires grad — the output of an eager trunk,
say: the step cannot return a gradient to it.  Detach it, or use
`make_step`, whose loss carries the input gradients.

examples:
>>> import lucid, lucid.nn as nn, lucid.nn.functional as F
>>> import lucid.optim as optim
>>> from lucid.compile import fused_step
>>> model = nn.Linear(8, 4).to('metal')
>>> opt = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
>>> step = fused_step(model, F.cross_entropy, opt)
>>> for batch in batches:
...     loss = step(batch.x, batch.target)       # one executable submission
notes:
A tensor requiring grad that `optimizer` does not hold — a loss weight left
out of it — is not stepped, and gets no `.grad`: the backward runs inside
the executable and the loss returned has no `grad_fn`.  Put it in the
optimizer, or use `make_step`.

Parameters on the CPU leave nothing to compile (the executables run on
Metal only): the call runs the eager step — `zero_grad()`, forward,
`backward()`, `optimizer.step()` of the optimizer passed in, which keeps
its own state — and returns the eager loss, with a one-time
`CompileFallbackWarning`.

see_also.name: translator that produces the update graph.

members.name: compile_optimizer
members.summary: Wrap `opt` so `opt.step()` runs as a single MPSGraph executable.
members.extended:
Dispatches on the concrete optimizer subclass and returns the
matching `_CompiledStepBase` subclass instance.  The
returned object exposes the same eager-optimizer API surface
(`step` / `zero_grad` / `param_groups` / `state_dict` /
`load_state_dict`) so existing training loops slot it in
without code changes — the only difference is that `step()`
runs as one compiled GPU kernel instead of N sequential per-
parameter element-wise updates.

Supported optimizers (13):
    * `lucid.optim.SGD` — classical, with optional
      momentum / Nesterov / weight-decay branches.
    * `lucid.optim.Adam`, `lucid.optim.AdamW` —
      bias-corrected first + second moments (AMSGrad too); coupled
      vs decoupled weight decay respectively.
    * `lucid.optim.RMSprop` — exponentially-smoothed
      squared gradient; `centered=True` keeps the running
      gradient mean as one more state buffer.
    * `lucid.optim.Adagrad`, `lucid.optim.Adadelta`,
      `lucid.optim.Adamax`, `lucid.optim.NAdam`,
      `lucid.optim.RAdam`, `lucid.optim.ASGD`,
      `lucid.optim.Rprop`, `lucid.optim.SparseAdam`
      — the eager update rule, with every step-dependent factor fed
      as a per-step scalar.
    * `lucid.optim.LBFGS` — a closure-less single-step
      subset (per-element Barzilai-Borwein direction); not the eager
      line-search algorithm.

Every parameter group compiles into the same executable: each
parameter reads its own group's hyper-parameters.

**One owner of the optimizer state at a time.**  Compiling hands the
state over to the wrapper: whatever `opt` built up in eager steps
so far is adopted, and from then on `opt.step()`,
`opt.state_dict()` and `opt.load_state_dict()` all go to the
wrapper — whichever handle the training loop holds (a loop driven by
`fused_step` only holds `opt`), it steps, saves and restores
the one state.  The checkpoint format is the eager one, so
checkpoints move freely between eager and compiled runs.  Compiling
the same optimizer again returns the same wrapper.

The exception is `lucid.optim.LBFGS`, whose compiled step is
a different algorithm: `opt` keeps its own eager state and methods,
and the wrapper's state is its own.

parameters.name: opt
parameters.description:
Concrete optimizer instance whose `step()` is being
lifted.  Held by reference; LR-scheduler callbacks and
other edits of `opt.param_groups` take effect on the next
step because the compiled step reads the groups every time.

returns.description:
Drop-in optimizer replacement.  The underlying class is one
of the `_Compiled<Name>` subclasses listed above.

raises.description:
When `opt` is not one of the supported optimizer classes —
the message lists the supported set.

examples:
Drop-in replacement:

    opt = lucid.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    sched = lucid.optim.lr_scheduler.StepLR(opt, step_size=10)
    copt = compile_optimizer(opt)

    for batch, target in loader:
        copt.zero_grad()
        loss = F.cross_entropy(model(batch), target)
        loss.backward()
        copt.step()             # one MPSGraph executable
        sched.step()            # seen by the next copt.step()

see_also.name: + update via the ghost-grad mechanism.  Use this when the
whole step is the unit of work and the model's forward
still lets loss.backward() run a regular eager

members.name: make_step
members.signature: make_step(model: Module, loss_fn: Callable[..., Tensor], dynamic: bool = False, segments: int | str = 1)
members.summary: Return a callable that runs one compiled training step.
members.extended:
The returned `step(x, *extra_inputs)` callable:

1. Calls `loss_fn(model(x), *extra_inputs)` once under
   `_tracing` to capture the op DAG (forward + loss).
2. Compiles a single MPSGraph executable that produces the loss
   and the gradient of the loss w.r.t. every model parameter and
   every input that requires grad, and every tensor the loss owns (a
   learned weight it closes over), via `compile_trace_with_backward`.
3. Runs the executable, populates a Lucid `autograd.Function`
   with the resulting (loss, grads) so the returned scalar loss has
   a working `grad_fn` and `loss.backward()` drives `.grad` on
   every parameter and loss weight — and on through an input computed
   by eager ops, so a compiled head trains the eager trunk that feeds it.
4. Caches the executable so a second call with the same input /
   parameter signature is a pure run.  Which inputs require grad is
   part of the signature: a step whose inputs need no gradient
   computes none.  A loss weight changing `requires_grad` retraces.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model whose forward will be traced + compiled.

parameters.name: loss_fn
parameters.description: `loss_fn(model_output, *extra_inputs) -> Tensor` scalar loss.

parameters.name: dynamic
parameters.description:
Accepted for API symmetry with `lucid.compile`, but the compiled
*training* step is always per-shape static: any batch size works (one
fwd+bwd executable per distinct shape), it just does not share a single
symbolic-batch executable across sizes.

parameters.name: segments
parameters.description:
Number of executable segments, a positive integer (default `1` — the
monolithic single executable described above).  When `> 1` and
`model` is an `nn.Sequential`, the model is split into that
many contiguous groups of children, each compiled into its own forward
+ backward executable and stitched with eager autograd
(`make_segmented_step`).  `"auto"` probes a few candidate counts
on the first batch and keeps the fastest (`make_autoseg_step`).

returns.description:
`step(x, *extra_inputs) -> Tensor` — the scalar loss.
`loss.backward()` works the same way as the eager baseline.

raises.description:
`segments` is neither an integer nor a string (a float, `None`, a
`bool`).
`segments` is below 1, or a string other than `"auto"`.

examples:
>>> import lucid, lucid.nn as nn, lucid.nn.functional as F
>>> import lucid.optim as optim
>>> from lucid.compile import make_step
>>> model = nn.Linear(8, 4).to('metal')
>>> step = make_step(model, lambda y, t: F.cross_entropy(y, t))
>>> opt = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
>>> for batch in batches:
...     opt.zero_grad()
...     loss = step(batch.x, batch.target)
...     loss.backward()
...     opt.step()
notes:
A step whose gradient passes through a custom
`lucid.autograd.Function` runs eagerly, with a one-time
`CompileFallbackWarning`: the executable can only differentiate the
ops `forward` recorded, and the `backward` the `Function` defines
— a straight-through estimator, a scaled or reversed gradient — would
not run.

see_also.name: the optimizer update into the same MPSGraph executable.
cached version of the same dispatch.

members.name: save_compiled
members.summary: Serialise a compiled forward graph to disk (AOT export).
members.extended:
Writes two files at `path`: `<path>.mpsgraphpackage` (Apple's
native MPSGraphExecutable archive, macOS 14+) and `<path>.meta`
(Lucid's I/O plan + dtype / shape / ABI metadata).  A
`CompiledModule` may hold multiple cached executables (one
per input signature); this entry point serialises the most recently
compiled one that has run — sufficient for AOT deployment where the
production input shape is fixed.

The on-disk artifact is identical to the per-process cache used
when `LUCID_COMPILE_DISK_CACHE=1` is set — so calls
`save_compiled` produces by hand are loadable by either
`load_compiled` or the runtime cache machinery.

> **Warning:**
>
> Saving always succeeds; **loading is what is restricted**.  A
> reloaded MPSGraph package does not report the feed order it
> expects, and that order only survives the round trip while every
> feed shares one shape and dtype.  An executable whose feeds
> differ — which includes every `lucid.nn.Module` with
> parameters, since the weights and the activations rarely share a
> shape — is refused by `load_compiled` rather than bound
> wrongly.  Until that is resolved, AOT export is usable for
> traced *functions* over uniform inputs, not for saving a trained
> model's forward pass.  Weights are not in the package either way:
> use `lucid.save` / `save_pretrained` for those.

parameters.name: cm
parameters.description:
A model wrapper returned by `lucid.compile`, called at least
once on Metal under `lucid.no_grad` (or
`lucid.inference_mode`): a call that needs gradients runs
eagerly and compiles nothing to save.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
Filesystem prefix.  Two files are written:
`f"{path}.mpsgraphpackage"` and `f"{path}.meta"`.

returns.description:
`True` on success.  Raises `RuntimeError` if no
executable of `cm` has run yet.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.compile as lc
>>> cm = lc.compile(lambda a, b: a * b + 1.0)
>>> a = lucid.randn(2, 8).to("metal")
>>> b = lucid.randn(2, 8).to("metal")
>>> _ = cm(a, b)                             # populate cache
>>> lc.save_compiled(cm, "/tmp/my_graph")    # writes .mpsgraphpackage + .meta
True

members.name: load_compiled
members.summary: Load a previously-saved compiled executable into a thin wrapper.
members.extended:
Returns an object exposing `__call__(*args)` that runs the saved
executable directly.  **The executable expects every feed in
feed order** — that includes both model parameters and runtime
inputs.  This is the raw artifact level: there is no automatic
parameter re-binding, because the saved package does not carry the
parameter *values* (only the graph structure + I/O ids).

For a smoother AOT workflow that re-binds parameters from a live
model, build a thin caller-side helper around `load_compiled`
that stitches `model.parameters()` onto the executable's feed
list before invocation.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
Filesystem prefix matching a previous `save_compiled`
call.  Expects both `<path>.mpsgraphpackage` and
`<path>.meta` to exist.

returns.description:
A callable wrapper.  Attributes:

* `num_inputs`: total feed count the executable expects.
* `input_ids`: ordered trace ids (debug / introspection).
* `__call__(*feeds)`: run with feeds in `input_ids` order.

raises.description:
The `.meta` sidecar is corrupted, the SDK ABI mismatches,
or the saved executable references engine internals that no
longer exist.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.compile as lc
>>> cm = lc.compile(lambda a, b: a * b + 1.0)
>>> a = lucid.randn(2, 8).to("metal")
>>> b = lucid.randn(2, 8).to("metal")
>>> _ = cm(a, b)                              # populate cache
>>> lc.save_compiled(cm, "/tmp/my_graph")
True
>>> step = lc.load_compiled("/tmp/my_graph")
>>> step.num_inputs                           # a and b, in first-read order
2
>>> out = step(a, b)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(out.to("cpu"), (a * b + 1.0).to("cpu")))
True

members.name: compile
members.signature: compile(model: Callable[P, R] | None = None, fullgraph: bool = False, dynamic: bool | None = None, backend: str | Callable[..., object] | None = None, mode: str | None = None, options: _CompileOptions | None = None, disable: bool = False)
members.summary: Wrap `model` so calls are routed through cached MPSGraph executables.
members.extended:
Accepts three call styles:

* **Module wrapping** — `lucid.compile(model)` returns a
  `CompiledModule` that delegates parameter walks /
  `state_dict` / device moves to `model` while routing
  `__call__` through an executable cache.
* **Plain callable wrapping** — `lucid.compile(fn)` where `fn`
  is a regular function or any callable.  Returns a thin wrapper
  whose `__call__` traces the function's body on the first
  invocation with a new input signature and caches an executable;
  it has no parameters of its own — pure tensor-in / tensor-out.
* **Decorator usage** — `@lucid.compile` on a function (or
  `@lucid.compile(dynamic=True)` factory form) — identical to
  the plain-callable form above but lets the user opt-in inline.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
Either an `nn.Module` instance (preferred when the
compiled unit carries learnable parameters) or any callable
whose signature is `(*tensor_args) -> Tensor | tuple | dict`.
When `None`, returns a decorator factory.

parameters.name: fullgraph
parameters.description: Compatibility flag with the reference signature.  Default `False`.

parameters.name: dynamic
parameters.description:
Treat the leading (batch) axis as symbolic so calls differing only
in batch size share **one** compiled executable (no recompile per
batch).  Default `None` (treated as `False`).

parameters.name: backend
parameters.description: Compatibility flag with the reference signature.  Default `None`.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Compatibility flag with the reference signature.  Default `None`.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Compatibility flag with the reference signature.  Default `None`.

parameters.name: disable
parameters.description:
When `True`, makes `compile` a no-op returning `model`
unchanged.  Default `False`.

returns.description:
A wrapper exposing the cache + run path.  When `model` was a
Module the wrapper re-exposes the inner module's
`parameters` / `state_dict` / training mode; when it was a
plain callable those return empty sequences.

notes:
* A call the compiler cannot lower, or one that needs gradients (see
  `CompiledModule`), runs eagerly with a one-time `UserWarning`
  naming why; `LUCID_COMPILE_VERBOSE=1` reports every occurrence.
* Attention lowers to a matmul-softmax-matmul decomposition, which
  materialises the score matrix; eager Metal's fused kernel never
  does.  A call whose attention would write more than 512 MiB of
  scores therefore runs eagerly, with a one-time notice — on an M4 Max
  a diffusion-transformer block at 18 720 keys took 120.8 ms compiled
  and 87.5 ms eager, and MPSGraph's own fused attention
  (`LUCID_COMPILE_FUSED_SDPA=1`) did not close the gap.
  `LUCID_COMPILE_LONG_ATTENTION=compile` keeps such calls compiled.

see_also.name: CompiledModule
see_also.description: the wrapper class returned by this function.

see_also.name: for an even tighter training loop.

summary: lucid.compile — graph-capture compile path for Apple Silicon.
extended:
Lowers a Lucid model's forward pass (and optionally its backward +
optimizer-update graph) into a single `MPSGraphExecutable`
that is cached per input signature.  Subsequent calls with the same
signature reuse the cached executable, skipping Python dispatch
entirely for every op inside the captured region.
notes:
* `compile` — the top-level entry.  Wraps either an
  `nn.Module` or a plain callable; returns a
  `CompiledModule`.  Also usable as a decorator
  (`@lucid.compile` or `@lucid.compile(dynamic=False)`).
* `CompiledModule` — module-shaped wrapper exposing
  `cache_info()` / `timing()` / `clear_cache()` plus
  `model`-delegated APIs (`parameters` / `state_dict` / `to`
  / `train` / `eval`).
* `compile_optimizer` — wraps the *update* step of an optimizer
  into a single cached executable (8 optimizers supported; see
  `lucid.compile._optim.compiler`).  Forward + backward stay eager.
* `fused_step` — single executable covering forward + loss +
  backward (via MPSGraph autodiff) + optimizer update via the
  ghost-grad placeholder mechanism.
* `compiled_step` — convenience wrapper combining
  `compile` + `make_step` for one-line training loops.
* `compiled_decode_step` — one cached executable per decode step of an
  autoregressive model over a `StaticCache`; what
  `generate(cache_implementation="compiled")` uses (LCD-660).
* `_tracing` — low-level context manager that installs a
  thread-local `Tracer`; used internally by every entry above.
  Public-but-underscored so external callers know they're touching
  an unstable surface.

The MPSGraph builder + executable cache + per-op emitters live in
`lucid/_C/compile/`.  The fallback policy is in `compile`'s
notes: a call that needs gradients, or that the compiler cannot lower,
runs eagerly.

Forward hooks and pre-hooks are traced with the forward only when lucid itself
declares them pure tensor rewrites (the prompt-learning sites of `lucid.peft`);
the hook set and the state such a hook reads are part of the cache key, so
adding, removing or reordering one retraces.  Any other forward hook or pre-hook
may act by side effect - log, count, record - which a replay would silently
skip, so a call with one runs eagerly, with a one-time notice.  Backward hooks,
global module hooks and tensor gradient hooks always run eagerly.
